4.text: Schools. — A few words will not be amiss regarding the Kolyma schools.

5.text: There are schools in Sredne-Kolymsk and Nishne-Kolymsk, and even in

6.text: Piatistennoye on the Large Anui River. All of them are parish schools.

7.text: The teaching is of such a kind, that the children have to be brought there

8.text: by requisition; although at the same time every private attempt at teaching

9.text: (by political exiles) finds pupils enough, and even pays. Among others, the

10.text: Yakut clans of Sredne-Kolymsk are obliged to send pupils to the school of

11.text: the town. They send orphans and children of the poorest people. Some

12.text: of these somehow learn to read and write without having learned the Russian

13.text: language; so that on the Kolyma one may sometimes see the strange sight of

14.text: a half savage man reading aloud a letter in a language almost wholly unknown

15.text: to himself, for the benefit of a Russian creole who knows the language, but

17.text: Scientific Expeditions. — Even scientific expeditions arranged by the

18.text: Government, when going to these remote countries, too often only served to

19.text: increase the oppression of the inhabitants, Russians and natives. Slovtzov

20.text: mentions one of the first instances of this. Gmelin and Müller, in 1735,

21.text: when leaving Irkutsk for Lake Baikal with light baggage, were not contented

22.text: with the thirty-seven horses assigned to them by the authorities, but sent their

23.text: men to the market-place and ordered them to capture more horses. They

24.text: started from the station Goloustnaia with a hundred and fifty horses. All

25.text: these horses were not paid for. They were delivered on requisition. For

26.text: the expedition of Bering, enormous quantities of provisions and ammunition

27.text: were dragged by the Yakut through the whole Yakutsk Province to Okhotsk.

28.text: Most of the horses perished on the way. To this Slovtzov adds, “No expe-

29.text: dition of such greatness and fame had, up to that time, gone through all

30.text: Siberia. God grant that, out of compassion for the poor country, future times

31.text: may never know a fame so ruinous!”¹ Of all the expeditions of former times

32.text: that visited the Kolyma country, that of Baron Wrangell (1820–24) seems

33.text: to have been the most scrupulous and sober-minded. Still local tradition

34.text: looks upon this expedition in a light very similar to that given in the opinion
